annotation.title_clean: Exploring the ethical sensitivity of Ph.D. students in robotics
annotation.title_en: Exploring the ethical sensitivity of Ph.D. students in robotics
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Battistuzzi, L.; Grassi, L.; Sgorbissa, A.
annotation.summary_en: Qualitative study of 21 first-year robotics Ph.D. students at the University of Genoa, using disaster-robotics vignettes to assess their ethical sensitivity. It argues ethical sensitivity is neglected in robotics and should be trained, as a step toward an online ethics training module for roboticists.
key_provisions_or_claims: Ethical sensitivity has received little attention in the robotics community.
Vignettes on disaster robotics (drones) were used to elicit students' recognition of ethical issues.
Students' recognition of ethical concerns varied across vignettes, e.g. 19 of 21 recognised privacy issues in vignette 4.
Promoting ethical sensitivity among roboticists is imperative.
Findings inform the design of an interactive online ethics training module.
